answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by making trust grown, not bought. A newcomer gains standing only through endorsements from established agents far apart in the trust graph, like vines spread across a trellis, so one operator cannot vouch for its own clones. Each sponsor holds a few endorsement slots that refill slowly, and each endorsement expires unless the newcomer keeps doing work, as a sonnet holds only when every line earns its place. An orchard works the same way: the tenth fake identity costs far more than the first, needing more distant sponsors spending scarcer slots.
